activity.notes: Simeon I ruled Bulgaria continuously from 893 until his death in 927, a reign conventionally associated with the First Bulgarian Empire's political and cultural Golden Age. His titulature developed during the reign, culminating in an imperial claim; ATLAS keeps one continuous sovereign Activity under the normalized role Tsar rather than splitting the same reign solely because his formal style changed.

sources.title: History of Bulgaria
sources.citation_text: The Council of Ministers of Bulgaria identifies 893–927 as the reign of Simeon the Great and the Golden Age of the First Bulgarian Empire.

sources.title: History of Bulgaria
sources.citation_text: The Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs identifies Tsar Simeon I's reign as 893–927 and describes Bulgaria's political, territorial, and cultural expansion under him.

sources.title: Symeon I – Prosopography of the Byzantine Empire
sources.citation_text: The Prosopography of the Byzantine Empire records Symeon as ruler of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.
